articles.title: 'I love doing dishes' at home and in the restaurant, says Culinary Class Wars’ Chef Son Jong-won
articles.summary: The Michelin-starred Korean chef and Chef & My Fridge regular reveals what’s always in his own refrigerator, the fridge red flag he hopes never to encounter – and the household chore he’d happily do forever. 'I love doing dishes' at home and in the restaurant, says Culinary Class Wars’ Chef Son Jong-won.

articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court clears way for Tennessee woman's imminent execution
articles.summary: A decision by the U. S. Supreme Court late on September 30 cleared the way for Christa Pike to be given a lethal injection after hours of dramatic legal wrangling up and down the judicial system U. S. Supreme Court clears way for Tennessee woman's imminent execution.

articles.title: Pilot stabbed colleague in bid to crash Israel-bound flydubai plane: Netanyahu
articles.summary: ‘The naive notion that our enemies cherish life and that we should pity them received another reminder this morning in the form of a terrorist who planned to crash a plane and murder the 180 Israelis on board,’ Itamar Ben Gvir said Israel-bound flydubai plane rerouted, pilots wounded in reported fight. articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
articles.summary: Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a massive $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner.

articles.title: Japan forms first national intelligence agency, eyes its own CIA
articles.summary: The demand for the overhaul of intelligence gathering network of Japan has gained strength in recent months amidst allegations that foreign powers like the U. S., Russia and China have been using Japan for their intelligence operations and that Japan is uncomfortable about such foreign operations on its soil. Japan forms first national intelligence agency, eyes its own CIA.

articles.title: Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation
articles.summary: Oleshky, a Ukrainian city occupied by Russian forces 9 kilometers from Kherson, is on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe. Since 2023, the city has been without electricity, gas, or drinking water. Now, Ukrainian teams are airlifting food supplies into the embattled area. Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation.

articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
articles.summary: President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of womenSouth Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unso.

articles.title: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion
articles.summary: Artificial Intelligence or AI – and the technology behind it – is moving fast. The question being asked across the world is who gets a seat at the table deciding how it's used and who gets to benefit. Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion.

articles.title: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban
articles.summary: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday. Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban.

articles.title: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
articles.summary: Homicide rates are falling across much of the world, but organised crime is on the rise in many regions as criminal networks diversify into trafficking, migrant smuggling, and the exploitation of natural resources, a new UN report launched on Wednesday revealed. Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked.

articles.title: Pakistan Orders Afghan Medical Students To Leave. Courts Push Back
articles.summary: Hundreds of Afghan medical students in Pakistan face expulsion, including women and students nearing graduation. Courts in several parts of the country have temporarily allowed them to stay and continue their studies, but their long-term future remains uncertain. Pakistan Orders Afghan Medical Students To Leave. Courts Push Back.

articles.title: AI tool that copied actor’s ‘lustrous’ voice violated his rights, Tokyo court rules
articles.summary: Kenjiro Tsuda wins case against TikTok account in landmark Japanese verdict to protect publicity rightsA court in Japan has ruled that the human voice has legal protection after a landmark case involving a well-known actor and a TikTok account that he claimed had cloned his “lustrous” baritone voice in its AI-generated videos. AI tool that copied actor’s ‘lustrous’ voice violated his rights, Tokyo court rules.

articles.title: Former US Diplomat Fried Warns Mixed Signals Could Undercut Russia Sanctions
articles.summary: The United States has new powers to increase economic pressure on Russia, but their impact will depend on whether the Trump administration uses them consistently and makes clear what it wants Moscow and other governments to do, former US diplomat Daniel Fried told RFE/RL. Former US Diplomat Fried Warns Mixed Signals Could Undercut Russia Sanctions.

articles.title: 'Right Moment Is Now' To Implement New Russia Sanctions Law
articles.summary: In an interview with RFE/RL, Daniel Fried, a former US ambassador and assistant secretary of state, said that the new sanctions law gives Washington leverage by exerting pressure on buyers of Russian oil and gas -- if the Trump administration is serious about implementing it. 'Right Moment Is Now' To Implement New Russia Sanctions Law.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit’s real test will come in the months ahead
articles.summary: For years, relations between Washington and Beijing seemed stuck on an escalation treadmill. Every quarter brought new semiconductor restrictions, naval jockeying in the South China Sea or retaliatory tariffs, locking the world’s two preeminent powers in an apparently irreversible downward spiral. articles.summary: Recent warnings from American AI leaders have created the impression that the world is only beginning to confront the dangers of advanced artificial intelligence. Dario Amodei, chief executive of tech company Anthropic, has called for governments to intervene to slow the development of increasingly powerful AI models. articles.title: Iran Threatens Energy Sites, Pens Letter To US Voters As It Awaits Official Response To Plan
articles.summary: Iran threatened to attack energy infrastructure across the Middle East if its security isn't guaranteed as it ratcheted up its rhetoric while waiting for the United States to officially respond to a plan Tehran says would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran Threatens Energy Sites, Pens Letter To US Voters As It Awaits Official Response To Plan.

articles.title: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
articles.summary: The Security Council is meeting in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors are likely to focus on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda, and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record. DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis.

articles.title: As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers
articles.summary: A new wave of deadly Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities is fueling bipartisan calls in Washington for US President Donald Trump to use sweeping new sanctions powers against Moscow, with lawmakers arguing that greater economic pressure could strengthen efforts to end the war. As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Warns Of New Russian Mobilization, 10,000 North Korean Troop Deployment
articles.summary: The death toll from Russia’s jet-powered drone attacks mounted in Ukraine while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that the Kremlin is preparing for a new mobilization at home and a fresh deployment of 10,000 North Korean troops. Zelenskyy Warns Of New Russian Mobilization, 10,000 North Korean Troop Deployment.

articles.summary: On 12 April 2026, the Pentagon announced that Elon Musk would head Project Meridian, a new initiative to embed artificial intelligence and space‑based assets into U. S. military operations. The program will allocate $2 billion over five years to develop autonomous drones, satellite‑linked targeting systems, and secure communications for the Army and Navy. Musk will coordinate with SpaceX, Tesla, and Neuralink to integrate satellite constellations, electric propulsion, and brain‑computer interfaces into defense platforms. The move signals a shift toward commercial‑private sector leadership in national security and aims to keep U. S. forces ahead of emerging adversaries.
